name: Brotli

name: Pcodec (Pco)
description: Lossless codec purpose-built for numerical (integer/float) sequences. Detects an approximate numeric structure per chunk (e.g. an integer multiplier/GCD, or an additive base), splits each value into 1-2 decorrelated "latent" integers along that structure, and entropy-codes the latents with an adaptive binning scheme that converges quickly to their true entropy.

pipeline.note: Selected at runtime based on the data's spatial/temporal smoothness pattern
pipeline.moreInfo: VQ predicts purely from spatial information, so every snapshot decompresses independently with no cross-snapshot dependency -- best for datasets with very low smoothness in the time dimension. VQT bootstraps the buffer with a VQ prediction on the first snapshot, then predicts every remaining snapshot from the corresponding point in the previous snapshot (an ordinary time-based predictor) -- designed for datasets with smooth time dimension that also have strong multi-peak-distribution patterns in space. MT bootstraps with a specialized 'initial-time-based' prediction on the first snapshot, then applies the same ordinary time-based predictor as VQT to the rest -- particularly effective on datasets with very high smoothness in the time dimension.

alternatives.name: MT

name: LCP
description: Error-bounded lossy compressor for particle/point data (molecular dynamics, cosmology, CFD, geology) that has no regular array structure for neighbor-based predictors to exploit. LCP-S, its single-frame spatial compressor, partitions 3D space into fixed-size grid cells sized directly from the error bound and represents each particle as (cell id, quantized in-cell offset) rather than a predicted residual; block metadata (ids, particle counts, relative coordinates) is then delta-coded, entropy-coded, and Zstd-compressed. For multi-frame data, LCP additionally offers a temporal mode (LCP-T) and picks between the two per frame via a finite-state machine that estimates compressed size — only the spatial (LCP-S) path is modeled here in detail.

pipeline.description: Quantizes each coordinate via error-bound-sized floor division, which simultaneously assigns particles to fixed-size 3D grid cells and bounds each coordinate's reconstruction error to the target bound.

pipeline.name: Block Metadata Coding
pipeline.description: Delta-codes each non-empty block's id, particle count, and its particles' relative in-cell coordinates.

pipeline.name: Entropy Coding
pipeline.description: Huffman- or fixed-length-codes the delta-coded metadata streams.

pipeline.name: Zstandard
pipeline.description: Final dictionary-compression pass over the encoded streams.

name: PNG (Portable Network Graphics)
description: Lossless raster image format. Each scanline is predicted by one of five per-pixel filter types (None, Sub, Up, Average, Paeth), chosen per row by the encoder to minimize residual magnitude, then the filtered byte stream is compressed with DEFLATE (LZ77 + Huffman).

pipeline.name: Scanline Filtering
pipeline.variant: 1 of 5 per-scanline filter types (None/Sub/Up/Average/Paeth); Paeth is the general 3-neighbor case
pipeline.description: Predicts each byte from its left/above/upper-left neighbors within the same channel plane; the encoder picks whichever filter type minimizes the row's residual magnitude, on a per-scanline basis.

pipeline.name: DEFLATE
pipeline.description: Compresses the filtered byte stream with LZ77 dictionary matching followed by Huffman entropy coding.

name: GIF (Graphics Interchange Format)
description: Palette-indexed raster/animation format. Pixels are stored as indices into a palette of at most 256 colors, then the index stream is compressed with LZW (Lempel-Ziv-Welch) dictionary coding. Compression of the index stream itself is lossless; converting a full-color source image down to a 256-color palette (when needed) is a separate, optional lossy step.

pipeline.name: Palette / Color Quantization
pipeline.note: Only needed when the source has more than 256 colors; skipped for images already palette-indexed
pipeline.description: Maps each pixel to the nearest color in a palette of at most 256 entries, via nearest-color matching or dithering.

pipeline.name: LZW Coding
pipeline.description: Encodes the palette-index stream with a growing dictionary of previously-seen substrings, each replaced by a code whose bit width increases as the dictionary fills.

name: WebP (Lossless)
description: Google's lossless raster format. Predicts each pixel from a per-block-selected spatial predictor (one of 14 modes), applies a reversible color transform (subtract-green plus optional cross-channel decorrelation), matches repeated pixel runs with a custom LZ77-style 'backward reference' stage, then entropy-codes the result with multiple adaptively-built Huffman trees.

pipeline.name: Spatial Prediction
pipeline.variant: 1 of 14 per-block predictor modes (WebP's own mode set; several are 2-neighbor blends in the same spirit as Lorenzo)
pipeline.description: Predicts each pixel from nearby already-decoded pixels; the encoder selects the best-fitting mode per block.

pipeline.name: Subtract-Green Transform
pipeline.description: Reversible integer transform (red -= green, blue -= green) that removes redundancy between color channels ahead of entropy coding.

pipeline.name: Backward Reference Coding
pipeline.description: Custom LZ77-style match stage exploiting repeated pixel runs, with its own match/distance encoding distinct from DEFLATE's.

pipeline.name: Huffman Coding
pipeline.description: Per-image, multiple adaptively-built Huffman trees (up to 5 symbol groups) encode the literal/length/distance/color-cache symbol stream.

name: WebP (Lossy)
description: Google's lossy raster format, built on VP8's intra-frame coding tools applied to a single still image. Converts to a fixed 4:2:0 YUV, predicts each block from its top/left neighbors using one of several directional intra modes, transforms residuals with a 4×4 DCT (plus a Walsh-Hadamard pass over the DC coefficients of 16×16-mode luma blocks), quantizes, zigzag-scans, and entropy-codes with a boolean arithmetic coder — then runs an in-loop deblocking filter whose output becomes the reference for any dependent blocks.

pipeline.name: RGB to YUV
pipeline.description: Converts source pixels to a luma/chroma representation.

pipeline.name: Chroma Subsampling
pipeline.description: Reduces chroma (U/V) resolution relative to luma (Y); unlike JPEG's optional subsampling ratios, WebP lossy always uses 4:2:0.

pipeline.name: Block Partitioning
pipeline.description: Splits each frame into 16×16 macroblocks, each further splittable into 4×4 luma sub-blocks for prediction and transform.

pipeline.name: Intra Prediction
pipeline.variant: ~10 modes across 16×16 luma, 4×4 luma, and 8×8 chroma block sizes
pipeline.description: Predicts each block from its already-decoded top/left neighbor edge; the encoder signals the best-fitting mode per block.

pipeline.name: 4×4 DCT
pipeline.description: Transforms each 4×4 residual block into frequency coefficients.

pipeline.name: Luma DC Hadamard
pipeline.note: Only for 16×16-mode luma blocks
pipeline.description: A second 4×4 Walsh-Hadamard pass over the grid of 16 luma DC coefficients, exploiting correlation between neighboring blocks' average intensity when the whole macroblock uses one prediction mode.

pipeline.name: Coefficient Quantization
pipeline.description: Quantizes DCT/Hadamard coefficients against an index-selected step size — the format's lossy step.

pipeline.name: Zigzag Scan
pipeline.description: Reorders each 4×4 block's quantized coefficients from low to high frequency.

pipeline.name: Boolean Entropy Coding
pipeline.variant: binary (boolean) arithmetic coder with per-context adaptive probabilities
pipeline.description: Entropy-codes coefficients and mode decisions as a sequence of binary decisions under adaptively-estimated probabilities.

pipeline.name: Loop Filter
pipeline.variant: VP8 deblocking filter (simple or normal mode)
pipeline.description: Smooths 4×4/16×16 block-boundary discontinuities; the filtered frame is what any block predicted from it will actually reference.

name: JPEG (Baseline Sequential)
description: The classic lossy raster codec (ITU-T T.81 / ISO/IEC 10918-1), baseline profile. Converts to YCbCr and optionally subsamples chroma, splits into 8×8 blocks, applies a 2D DCT, quantizes coefficients against a quality-scaled table, reorders coefficients in zigzag scan order, differentially codes the DC coefficient against the previous block, run-length-codes zero AC coefficients, and entropy-codes the result with Huffman coding.

pipeline.name: RGB to YCbCr
pipeline.description: Converts source pixels to luma/chroma before subsampling and transform.

pipeline.name: Chroma Subsampling
pipeline.description: Reduces chroma (Cb/Cr) resolution relative to luma (Y); human vision is far less sensitive to color resolution than brightness resolution.

pipeline.name: 8×8 Block Splitting
pipeline.description: Partitions each channel plane into non-overlapping 8×8 pixel blocks, processed independently by the stages below.

pipeline.name: Discrete Cosine Transform
pipeline.description: 2D 8×8 DCT decorrelates each block into frequency coefficients, concentrating energy into a few low-frequency terms.

pipeline.name: Coefficient Quantization
pipeline.description: Divides each frequency coefficient by a quality-scaled step from an 8×8 quantization table (finer steps at low frequency, coarser at high) and rounds — the format's lossy step.

pipeline.name: Zigzag Scan
pipeline.description: Reorders the 8×8 quantized coefficients from low to high frequency into a 1D sequence, clustering the trailing zeros the run-length stage below exploits.

pipeline.name: DC Prediction
pipeline.description: Codes each block's DC (average-intensity) coefficient as the difference from the previous block's DC value, since neighboring blocks' average brightness is usually similar.

pipeline.name: AC Run-Length Coding
pipeline.description: Encodes each nonzero AC coefficient as a (run-of-zeros, value) pair, exploiting the long zero runs zigzag ordering produces toward the high-frequency end.

pipeline.name: Entropy Coding
pipeline.description: Huffman-codes the (run, value) symbol stream; JPEG also defines an optional arithmetic-coding mode that saw little real-world adoption.

name: JPEG 2000
description: Wavelet-based raster codec (ISO/IEC 15444-1) offering both a lossy and a lossless profile from largely the same pipeline shape. The lossy (default) profile converts color with an irreversible transform, applies a multi-level 9/7 wavelet decomposition, quantizes each subband independently, then codes the result with EBCOT's context-adaptive embedded bitplane coder — producing a scalable bitstream a rate-distortion step can truncate to any target size. The lossless profile (see variants) swaps in an integer-exact reversible color transform and wavelet filter and skips quantization entirely.

pipeline.name: Color Transform (ICT)
pipeline.description: Floating-point YCbCr-like color decorrelation ahead of the wavelet transform.

pipeline.name: Tiling
pipeline.description: Partitions the image into independent rectangular tiles, each compressed separately.

pipeline.name: Discrete Wavelet Transform
pipeline.description: Multi-level 2D wavelet decomposition into frequency subbands; the 9/7 filter is not integer-exact, trading exact reversibility for better energy compaction than the lossless profile's 5/3 filter.

pipeline.name: Subband Quantization
pipeline.variant: scalar deadzone quantization, independent step size per subband
pipeline.description: Uniformly quantizes each subband's coefficients with its own step size and a widened deadzone bin around zero — the format's lossy step.

pipeline.name: EBCOT
pipeline.description: Codes each subband's code-blocks bitplane-by-bitplane with context-adaptive arithmetic coding, producing an embedded bitstream.
pipeline.note: Post-compression rate-distortion optimization (PCRD-opt) selects how many bitplanes of each code-block to keep to hit a target size/quality.

variants.name: Lossless (5/3 Reversible)
variants.description: Swaps the irreversible 9/7 wavelet and color transform for integer-exact reversible equivalents and skips quantization entirely, at a lower compression ratio than the lossy profile.

pipeline.name: Color Transform (RCT)
pipeline.description: Integer-exact, bit-reversible color decorrelation (as opposed to the primary pipeline's floating-point ICT).

pipeline.name: Tiling
pipeline.description: Partitions the image into independent rectangular tiles, each compressed separately.

pipeline.name: Discrete Wavelet Transform
pipeline.description: Integer lifting-scheme wavelet transform that is exactly invertible; no quantization stage follows.

pipeline.name: EBCOT
pipeline.description: Same embedded bitplane coder as the lossy pipeline, run to full bitplane depth (no rate truncation) for exact reconstruction.

name: EBCC
description: Error-bounded lossy compressor for weather and climate data, built as two layers: a JPEG 2000 base layer does the bulk lossy compression, then a residual layer wavelet-transforms and SPIHT-codes what JPEG 2000 got wrong, truncating that embedded bitstream once the target pointwise-absolute or range-relative error bound is met.

pipeline.name: JPEG 2000 Base Layer
pipeline.description: Wavelet-based lossy compression of the full array, providing the bulk of the size reduction

pipeline.name: Residual Discrete Wavelet Transform
pipeline.description: Applies a DWT to the residual (original data minus the JPEG 2000-reconstructed base layer) to decorrelate the remaining error before coding it

pipeline.name: SPIHT Residual Coding
pipeline.description: Encodes the residual's wavelet coefficients into a bitplane-ordered, hierarchically-partitioned embedded bitstream
pipeline.note: The bitstream is truncated once the target pointwise-absolute or range-relative error bound is met — the same embedded/early-stop principle as ZFP's group-tested RLE, achieved here via SPIHT's tree partitioning instead of bitplane run-length coding

name: MPEG-2 Video
description: ISO/IEC 13818-2 / ITU-T H.262, the video codec behind DVD and digital broadcast television. Each macroblock is predicted either directly (intra, I-frames — the raw pixel block is DCT-coded with no spatial predictor) or via block motion compensation from a previous and/or future reference frame (inter, P/B-frames); the residual is DCT-transformed, quantized, zigzag-scanned, and entropy-coded with fixed Huffman-style VLC tables. Unlike every later codec in this family, MPEG-2 has no in-loop filter — visible block edges are a well-known artifact of the format, and directional intra prediction (introduced with H.264) doesn't exist here either.

pipeline.name: RGB to YUV
pipeline.description: Converts to a luma/chroma representation; broadcast/production sources are typically captured directly in YUV, making this an implicit rather than an explicit encoder stage.

pipeline.name: Chroma Subsampling
pipeline.description: Reduces chroma resolution relative to luma.

pipeline.name: Macroblock Partitioning
pipeline.description: Splits each frame into 16×16 macroblocks, each holding four 8×8 luma blocks plus associated chroma blocks.

pipeline.name: Block Prediction
pipeline.description: I-frame macroblocks are coded with no spatial predictor at all; P/B-frame macroblocks are motion-compensated against reference frames.

alternatives.name: None (Intra)
alternatives.description: I-frame macroblocks are DCT-coded directly from raw pixels — MPEG-2 predates directional intra prediction entirely.

alternatives.name: Motion Compensation (Inter)
alternatives.description: P-frame macroblocks predict from one previous reference frame; B-frame macroblocks predict from a weighted combination of a previous and a future reference frame.

pipeline.name: 8×8 DCT
pipeline.description: Transforms each 8×8 luma/chroma block — the raw pixel block for intra, the motion-compensated residual for inter — into frequency coefficients.

pipeline.name: Coefficient Quantization
pipeline.description: Uniformly quantizes DCT coefficients against a step size derived from a per-macroblock quantizer scale.

pipeline.name: Zigzag Scan
pipeline.description: Reorders each block's quantized coefficients from low to high frequency.

pipeline.name: Intra DC Prediction
pipeline.note: Intra macroblocks only
pipeline.description: Differentially codes each intra block's DC coefficient against the previous block's DC value, the same DC-prediction trick JPEG uses; inter blocks' DCT is already applied to a near-zero-mean residual and skip this.

pipeline.name: Run-Level Coding
pipeline.description: Encodes each nonzero coefficient as a (run-of-zeros, level) pair.

pipeline.name: VLC Entropy Coding
pipeline.description: Entropy-codes the (run, level) symbol stream and motion vectors with standard fixed VLC tables — no adaptive/context-based coding, unlike every later codec here.

name: H.264 / AVC
description: ITU-T H.264 / ISO/IEC 14496-10 (AVC), the dominant deployed video codec. Each macroblock is predicted either from decoded spatial neighbors (directional intra prediction, introduced with this standard) or via motion compensation from a previously-decoded reference frame (inter); the residual is transformed with a 4×4 or 8×8 integer DCT-like transform (plus a Hadamard pass over luma/chroma DC coefficients for whole-macroblock intra modes), quantized, scanned, and entropy-coded. The Main/High profiles use context-adaptive binary arithmetic coding (CABAC); the Baseline profile (see variants) instead uses simpler context-adaptive VLC (CAVLC). An in-loop deblocking filter smooths block edges before the frame is stored as a prediction reference.

name: H.265 / HEVC
description: ITU-T H.265 / ISO/IEC 23008-2, H.264's successor, targeting roughly half the bitrate at equal quality. Two in-loop filters run in sequence: deblocking, then Sample Adaptive Offset (SAO).

name: VP9
description: Google's royalty-free successor to VP8 (WebP-lossy's basis), roughly competitive with HEVC. Splits each frame into 64×64 superblocks recursively partitioned down to 4×4, predicts each block via directional intra prediction or motion compensation (with up to 3 reference frames), transforms residuals with a selectable DCT/ADST combination, quantizes, and entropy-codes with a non-adaptive-within-frame boolean coder whose probabilities are updated between frames. A single in-loop deblocking filter runs before the frame is stored as a reference.

name: AV1
description: The Alliance for Open Media's royalty-free codec, roughly 30% more efficient than HEVC/VP9. Splits each frame into 128×128 superblocks recursively partitioned via an extended tree, predicts each block via a much richer directional intra mode set or motion compensation (with up to 7 reference frames and warped/OBMC prediction), applies an extensible transform kit (DCT/ADST/flip-ADST/identity, size- and mode-dependent) chosen per block, quantizes, and entropy-codes with a multi-symbol adaptive range coder whose per-context probabilities update continuously. Three in-loop filters run in sequence: deblocking, CDEF (a directional deringing filter), and loop restoration.

name: TZ
description: GPU-native error-bounded lossy compressor that replaces the block-wise spatial decomposition used by other GPU compressors with a single global Tucker decomposition, computed using an adaptive randomized SVD engine. By prioritizing global spectral energy compaction over local, per-block approximation, TZ captures correlations that block-decomposed methods fragment, and its global processing enables a unified quantization/coding scheme with no block artifacts or per-block metadata overhead.

pipeline.name: Adaptive Randomized ST-HOSVD
pipeline.moreInfo: Iteratively unfolds the input tensor and adaptively extracts singular values with respect to the error bound using a randomized SVD with rank finding, to produce one global core tensor plus one factor matrix per dimension.

pipeline.name: Equivalent Weighting
pipeline.moreInfo: Scales the factor matrices by their singular-value energy contribution ahead of quantization, so a uniform quantization step afterward distributes error proportionally to each component's significance.
